proof:
Source: step 3 of the parent proof; Simon 6.2.24(1) (chapter-06.txt line 414: ∂f_#T = f_#∂T), extended from smooth f to C¹ f through 2.24(2) (lines 415–425) by approximating φ with smooth maps; details filled in. Notation: E := ℝ^P; μ := H^n⌞M; for a smooth map χ : E → E and a form α of degree d, χ^#α(x) := α(χ(x))∘Dχ(x) (= SimonGMT pullbackFormWithin univ χ α, since fderivWithin on univ is fderiv, fderivWithin_univ); d := exteriorDerivative = extDeriv.
1. Reduction. If n = 0, BoundaryVanishes S is True by definition. Let n = m + 1 and assume T.boundary = 0. By extensionality of currents (GeometricCurrentOn.ext) it suffices to prove S.boundary(η) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U). By GeometricCurrentOn.boundary_apply, S.boundary(η) = S(exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η), the test form whose underlying form is dη. Fix η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
2. Smooth approximants. By the sibling dpf_smooth_approx_compact_perturbation (U open, K compact ⊆ U, φ C¹, φ = id off K) there are C^∞ maps ψ_k, a compact K' ⊆ U and C ∈ ℝ with ψ_k = id off K', ‖Dψ_k(x)‖ ≤ C for all k, x (so C ≥ 0), ψ_k(x) → φ(x) and Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x) for every x.
3. Pulled-back test forms. Let α ∈ {η, dη}; α is C^∞ with compact support in U (exteriorDerivative_isTestForm, tsupport_exteriorDerivative_subset). The form ψ_k^#α is C^∞: ψ_k^#α(x) = (compContinuousLinearMapCLM (Dψ_k(x))) (α(ψ_k(x))); x ↦ α(ψ_k(x)) is C^∞ (ContDiff.comp), x ↦ Dψ_k(x) is C^∞ (ContDiff.fderiv_right), L ↦ compContinuousLinearMapCLM L is analytic on all of End(E) (Mathlib ContinuousAlternatingMap.analyticOnNhd_compContinuousLinearMapCLM), hence C^∞ (AnalyticOnNhd.contDiffOn with uniqueDiffOn_univ), and applying a C^∞ family of continuous linear maps to a C^∞ family of vectors is C^∞ (ContDiff.clm_apply). Support: let F₀ := tsupport α ∪ K', a compact subset of U. If x ∉ F₀, the open set W := E ∖ F₀ is a neighbourhood of x on which ψ_k = id, so Dψ_k = I on W and ψ_k^#α(z) = α(z) = 0 for z ∈ W; hence tsupport(ψ_k^#α) ⊆ F₀ ⊆ U and ψ_k^#α has compact support. Therefore ψ_k^#η ∈ 𝒟^m(U) and ψ_k^#(dη) ∈ 𝒟^n(U).
4. Naturality of d. d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη) as forms on E: this is SimonGMT exteriorDerivativeOn_pullbackFormWithin with domains univ (open), ψ_k C^∞ on univ, MapsTo univ univ and η smooth (it rests on Mathlib extDerivWithin_pullback), together with the identifications exteriorDerivativeOn univ α = extDerivWithin α univ = extDeriv α = dα (Mathlib extDerivWithin_univ) and pullbackFormWithin univ ψ_k α = ψ_k^#α (Mathlib fderivWithin_univ). So exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m (ψ_k^#η) is the test form ψ_k^#(dη) (Subtype.ext).
5. The approximating values vanish. Since T.boundary = 0 and R represents T: 0 = T.boundary(ψ_k^#η) = T(d(ψ_k^#η)) = T(ψ_k^#(dη)) = R.action(ψ_k^#(dη)) = ∫_M θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) dH^n(x) =: I_k for every k.
6. Dominated convergence. Put h_k(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x)) and h(x) := θ(x) ξ(x)(dη(φ(x))∘Dφ(x)).
 (a) Measurability: each h_k and h is μ-a.e. strongly measurable (θ measurable, ξ μ-a.e. strongly measurable, the covector fields x ↦ dη(ψ_k(x))∘Dψ_k(x) and x ↦ dη(φ(x))∘Dφ(x) continuous because dη, ψ_k, φ, Dψ_k and Dφ are continuous and (β, L) ↦ β∘L is jointly continuous, ContinuousAlternatingMap.continuous_compContinuousLinearMapCLM, and evaluation is continuous bilinear).
 (b) Pointwise convergence: for every x, ψ_k(x) → φ(x) and dη is continuous, Dψ_k(x) → Dφ(x), (β, L) ↦ β∘L is jointly continuous and ξ(x) is continuous linear; so h_k(x) → h(x).
 (c) Domination: by R.orients, for μ-a.e. x, ξ(x)(β) = ±β(τ) with τ orthonormal, so |ξ(x)(β)| ≤ ‖β‖ (ContinuousAlternatingMap.le_opNorm). If h_k(x) ≠ 0 then ψ_k(x) ∈ tsupport(dη) ⊆ tsupport η, and if moreover x ∉ K' then x = ψ_k(x); so h_k(x) ≠ 0 implies x ∈ C₀ := tsupport η ∪ K', a compact subset of U. Using ‖β∘L‖ ≤ ‖β‖‖L‖^n (ContinuousAlternatingMap.norm_compContinuousLinearMap_le): |h_k(x)| ≤ C^n ‖dη‖_∞ θ(x) 1_{C₀}(x) for μ-a.e. x and all k (‖dη‖_∞ < ∞, dη continuous with compact support). The bound is μ-integrable since ∫_{M∩C₀} θ dH^n < ∞ (R.locallyIntegrable_mult).
 By dominated convergence (MeasureTheory.tendsto_integral_of_dominated_convergence), I_k → ∫_M h dH^n.
7. Conclusion. The hypothesis on S applied to the test form dη ∈ 𝒟^n(U) (= exteriorDerivativeTestOn U m η) gives S.boundary(η) = S(dη) = ∫_M h dH^n = lim_k I_k = 0 (step 5). Hence S.boundary(η) = 0 for every η, so S.boundary = 0, i.e. BoundaryVanishes S.
key_steps: n = 0 is trivial; for n = m+1 it suffices that S(dη) = 0 for every η ∈ 𝒟^m(U).
Take C^∞ maps ψ_k = id off a compact K' ⊆ U with uniformly bounded derivatives converging pointwise to φ, Dφ (sibling smooth_approximation).
ψ_k^#η and ψ_k^#(dη) are test forms in U, supported in tsupport η ∪ K'.
d(ψ_k^#η) = ψ_k^#(dη), so 0 = ∂T(ψ_k^#η) = ∫_M θ ξ(dη(ψ_k x)∘Dψ_k(x)) dH^n.
Dominated convergence (bound C^n‖dη‖_∞ θ 1_{tsupport η ∪ K'}) gives S(dη) = lim = 0.
